+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: '8380'
+title: A response in the thread shows each fenced code block in CodeBlockView
+---
+## What
+In the chat stream, a fenced code block of a response does not use ``CodeBlockView``. ``ResponseView`` (`Sources/AgentViewKit/Content/ResponseView.swift`, the `editor` property) shows all of the Markdown of a response in one ``RenderedMarkdownView`` (`Sources/AgentViewKit/Content/RenderedMarkdownView.swift`). EditorKit draws each fence inside that editor, with its own header (`editorCodeBlockHeader` and `CodeBlockHeaderView` in EditorKit `Sources/EditorSwiftUI/EditorCodeBlockHeader.swift`). That header is a bad near duplicate of the header of ``CodeBlockView`` (`Sources/AgentViewKit/Code/CodeBlockView.swift`): the grey language label does not align with the left edge of the code, the space above it is not the same as the space below it, and it has no line numbers and no Copy button. The user decided (2026-11-21): use ``CodeBlockView`` for each fence of a response.
+
+Approach:
+- [ ] Add `Sources/AgentViewKit/Content/MarkdownCodeFences.swift`: `nonisolated enum MarkdownCodeFences` with `static func segments(in markdown: String) -> [MarkdownSegment]`. `MarkdownSegment` is `.prose(String)` or `.code(code: String, language: String?, filename: String?)`. Use the CommonMark fence rules (a line of 3 or more backticks or tildes, up to 3 spaces of indent; the closing fence uses the same character and is not shorter). Read the language and the file name from the info string in the same way as EditorKit `FencedCodeBlock.language` and `FencedCodeBlock.fileName` (`../EditorKit/Sources/EditorText/Syntax/FencedCodeBlocks.swift`). A fence with no closing line (a response that still streams) is a `.code` segment that holds the lines up to the end of the text. Follow the style of `Sources/AgentViewKit/Content/MarkdownParagraphs.swift`.
+- [ ] In ``ResponseView``, show the segments in a `VStack(alignment: .leading)`: each `.prose` segment in a ``RenderedMarkdownView``, each `.code` segment in ``CodeBlockView``(code:language:filename:). A text with no fence keeps the current single ``RenderedMarkdownView`` and the current model cache path, so the current behavior of a response with no code does not change.
+- [ ] Give each segment a stable identity (its index in the segment list), so a streamed chunk that adds text to the last segment updates that segment and does not make new views for the segments before it.
+
+Out of scope (follow-up tasks, for `/plan`): one text selection across the prose and the code of one response (``ResponseSelectionClaim``), the Copy Code Block command (`AgentCommandVerb.copyCodeBlock`, which reads `CommandContext.codeBlock` from the EditorKit Markdown editor in `Sources/AgentViewKit/Commands/AgentCommands.swift`), citation paragraph indices across segments (``MarkdownParagraphs``), and transcript search marks in a code segment. ``AttachmentPreview`` and ``ConversationEmptyState`` keep ``RenderedMarkdownView`` as it is.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] `MarkdownCodeFences.segments(in: "Intro.\n\n```swift\nlet a = 1\n```\n\nEnd.")` returns three segments: `.prose("Intro.")`, `.code(code: "let a = 1", language: "swift", filename: nil)`, `.prose("End.")`.
+- [ ] A fence with no closing line gives a `.code` segment with all the lines after the opening fence.
+- [ ] A text with no fence gives exactly one `.prose` segment that is equal to the text.
+- [ ] A response with one fence shows one ``CodeBlockView`` (accessibility identifier `CodeBlockView.identifier`) that has the language label of the fence, and the prose before and after it in ``RenderedMarkdownView``.
+- [ ] A response with no fence shows one ``RenderedMarkdownView`` and no ``CodeBlockView``.
+- [ ] The current tests in `Tests/AgentViewKitTests/Content/ResponseViewTests.swift`, `Tests/AgentViewKitTests/Content/RenderedMarkdownViewTests.swift` and `Tests/AgentViewKitTests/Content/ResponseSelectionClaimTests.swift` pass with no change.
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] New `Tests/AgentViewKitTests/Content/MarkdownCodeFencesTests.swift`: backtick and tilde fences, a closing fence that is longer than the opening fence, an indented fence (up to 3 spaces), an info string with a language and a file name, an unclosed fence at the end, two fences one after the other, and a text with no fence.
+- [ ] `Tests/AgentViewKitTests/Content/ResponseViewTests.swift`: add tests that a response with one fence makes a prose, code, prose segment layout with a ``CodeBlockView`` for the code, and that a response with no fence makes one ``RenderedMarkdownView``. Use the same mount style as the tests in that file.
+- [ ] `ScreenshotTests/Tests/ScreenshotTests/HostedSnapshotTests.swift`: add a snapshot of a response with prose and one Swift fence, so the user can review the PNG. Only compile it (`cd ScreenshotTests && swift build --build-tests`); do not run the hosted suite.
+- [ ] Run `swift test` in the repo root. Expected: all tests pass, 0 failures.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass.
+- Run only the headless `swift test`. Do not run the IntegrationTests or ScreenshotTests suites (they take the screen focus); a build of them is allowed.
\ No newline at end of file
